reason: node-forge <=1.4.0 RSA signature-verification flaw; no patched release is available as of 2026-10-21. Present only in word-addin devDependencies through office-addin-dev-certs -> mkcert and office-addin-debugging -> office-addin-dev-settings -> @microsoft/m365agentstoolkit-cli -> @microsoft/teamsfx-core. Their local certificate helpers generate/sign certificates and parse local key/certificate files; they do not call the vulnerable signature verifier. The production add-in image contains only the static bundle and server.mjs (word-addin/Dockerfile), not these development dependencies. REMOVE WHEN: node-forge publishes a patched release and these chains can resolve it; reassess if the dependency gains a production or signature-verification caller.

braces <=3.0.3 stack-exhaustion DoS through deeply nested brace patterns; published 2026-09-18 and no patched release exists (3.0.3 is the latest braces). Present only in devDependencies: frontend through @ladle/react -> globby -> fast-glob -> micromatch, and word-addin through webpack-dev-server -> http-proxy-middleware -> micromatch (`npm ls braces --omit=dev` is empty in every workspace). Those callers expand glob and proxy-path patterns written in this repo's own config, rather than user or document input. The frontend Docker image currently retains development dependencies, so this package is present in that image; the exception relies on these tooling call sites and controlled pattern inputs, not on image exclusion. The production Word add-in image contains only the static bundle and server.mjs. REMOVE WHEN: braces publishes a patched release (or micromatch drops braces) and these chains resolve it; reassess if braces gains a production caller.

@azure/msal-node 5.0.0-beta.0 - 7.0.2 authorization-code flow may disclose parameters to an attacker-controlled endpoint; published after 2026-10-23's S6 audit. Present only in word-addin devDependencies through office-addin-debugging -> office-addin-dev-settings -> @microsoft/m365agentstoolkit-cli (and its @azure/identity), which pin ^6.0 while the fix exists only in 7.1.x (`npm ls @azure/msal-node --omit=dev` is empty). Those CLIs sideload the add-in on a developer machine; no CI job, test or production image runs them, and the production add-in image contains only the static bundle and server.mjs. REMOVE WHEN: the m365agentstoolkit-cli / @azure/identity chain inside office-addin-debugging's declared range accepts @azure/msal-node >=7.1; reassess if msal-node gains a production caller.
